ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Cross-Modal Contrastive Federated Learning
PROPOSAL: We design a federated learning framework, dubbed Cross-Modal Contrastive Federated Learning (CMCFL), which enables diverse users to collaboratively learn task-agnostic representations while preserving privacy. Users can choose any model architectures and tasks, and our framework leverages a variant of the InfoNCE loss, adapted to align the representations across all models simultaneously, using a mini-batch of samples from all users. During the training process, users locally compute the similarity between representations, while the server computes the contrastive loss based on the similarities. This ensures efficient and communication-friendly alignment across diverse task and architectural settings.
CONTROLS: We compare CMCFL to the previously proposed Gramian-based contrastive loss, and with the basic InfoNCE loss applied to every pair of models. We also compare to a baseline where no contrastive loss is applied, and a naive greedy approach where each user's model is aligned one at a time.
COST: 43200
PREDICTION: CMCFL outperforms the Gramian-based loss and the naive baseline, but falls short of achieving state-of-the-art performance compared to the InfoNCE loss applied to every pair of models. However, CMCFL significantly reduces the communication overhead of the InfoNCE baseline.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-modal Knowledge Distillation for Federated Multi-task Learning
PROPOSAL: Building upon CMCFL, we propose a multi-modal knowledge distillation (MMKD) framework to improve the efficiency and accuracy of federated multi-task learning. Each user participates in a shared mini-batch, and distills knowledge from experts in other tasks using a task-agnostic representation-based distillation loss. We adapt the knowledge distillation framework from multiple expert sources to the federated learning setting. Users can now learn from other users' expertise, fostering cross-task knowledge sharing. The MMKD module is integrated with the CMCFL framework, providing a trade-off between representation learning and knowledge distillation.
CONTROLS: We compare the MMKD framework to a basic knowledge distillation baseline where each user learns from only one other user, and to a variant of the InfoNCE loss that only accounts for the representations between pairs of users. We also ablate the MMKD framework to analyze its contribution to the overall performance.
COST: 64800
PREDICTION: MMKD improves the performance of federated multi-task learning by adaptively distilling knowledge from multiple users, without directly sharing task-specific data. However, its performance may degrade when users have very different task objectives, which can lead to suboptimal knowledge distillation.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Multi-modal Knowledge Distillation for Federated Multi-task Learning (Rev)
PROPOSAL: We revise the MMKD framework to enable more efficient and adaptive knowledge distillation across users with diverse task objectives and model architectures. We introduce a novel mechanism, called Attend-On-Demand, which selectively attentions the distillation process towards the users with more relevant expertise, as determined by a server-side clustering module. Users can now choose whether to attend, what to attend to, and when to attend in a fully distributed manner. This adaptation ensures that knowledge distillation remains effective even in cases of user heterogeneity.
CONTROLS: We maintain the same set of controls as before, with an additional ablation study on the Attend-On-Demand mechanism to assess its contribution.
COST: 60480
PREDICTION: The revised MMKD framework with Attend-On-Demand achieves better performance than the basic MMKD and InfoNCE baseline in heterogeneous settings, as it more effectively adapts to the diverse expertise of users. However, its added complexity may lead to increased computation time.

TITLE: Combining Instance-Dependent and Instance-Independent Label Noise Correction Methods
PROPOSAL: Building on the previous proposals, we explore the possibility of combining instance-dependent and instance-independent label noise correction methods to create a more robust and adaptable noise correction framework. This is achieved by using a weighted average of the probabilities learned from both methods, which are then used to correct the labels in the dataset. We evaluate the performance of this framework using a range of datasets and architectures, including ResNet-50 and EfficientNet-B0, and compare it to the previously proposed methods.

PROPOSAL: In this final proposal, we develop an automated label noise correction framework that can learn to correct noisy labels in real-world datasets without requiring explicit specification of noise patterns or distributions. We evaluate the performance of our framework on a range of real-world datasets, including ImageNet and CIFAR-10, and compare it to the previously proposed noise correction methods.

We'll meta-train a model selector using this dataset and then meta-test it on real-world datasets like CIFAR-10 (10% noisy labels) and WebVision (20% noisy labels).

Limited success on WebVision is a possible outcome, as the noise patterns in this dataset are highly instance-dependent.

TITLE:  End-to-End Noisy Label Correction via Meta Learning
PROPOSAL:  We propose to train an end-to-end meta-learning model that can learn to correct noisy labels. This model will first receive a set of labeled examples, a subset of which are subject to label noise, and output a set of corrected labels. The model will then be trained on its predictions and the true labels to adjust its parameters using a reward-based loss function. In one version, the reward function will be based on the model's confidence in its predictions. In another version, the reward function will depend on the ratio between the type of label produced and the amount of laboratory likelihood that anything occurring resembled the produced type based off the probabilities stored.

TITLE:  Semi-supervised Learning with Noisy Labels via Self-training and Knowledge Distillation
PROPOSAL:  We propose to improve the robustness of models to noisy labels by combining self-training and knowledge distillation strategies. First, we will train a teacher model using the noisy labels and use its predictions to generate pseudo-labels for the unlabelled data. Then, we will train a student model using these pseudo-labels and a knowledge distillation loss that combines the teacher's softmax output with a mean squared error loss. By iteratively improving the teacher and student models, we expect to learn a more robust model to noisy labels. To enhance this approach, we will also use a form of instance-dependent noise, by dynamically adjusting the level of noise injected into the pseudo-labels based on the strength of the teacher's predictions.
CONTROLS:  Our proposed method will be compared against standard self-training and knowledge distillation methods, as well as existing noisy label correction methods that incorporate a form of both strategies.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Effectiveness of Confidence-Based Label Filtering on Noisy-Labeled Datasets
PROPOSAL: Train ResNet-18 models on CIFAR-10-C (a noisy variation of CIFAR-10 with symmetric class-conditional noise) and CIFAR-100-C (a noisy variation of CIFAR-100 with symmetric class-conditional noise), using label filtering based on predicted confidence scores and comparing the performance to a baseline model trained without label filtering.
CONTROLS: Baseline model trained without label filtering, ablated models trained with different confidence threshold values.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: We expect to see improved performance with confidence-based label filtering, especially on more noisy data (CIFAR-100-C), but this may fail for very low or very high confidence threshold values, leading to under- or over-filtration.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Impact of Label Noise on the Generalization Performance of State-of-the-Art Models
PROPOSAL: Train Wide ResNet-50-2 models on noisy variations of ImageNet (ImageNet-C) with different levels of symmetric instance-dependent noise, and compare their generalization performance to a baseline model trained on clean ImageNet.
CONTROLS: Baseline model trained on clean ImageNet, ablated models trained with different levels of label noise, and models trained with different robust loss functions (e.g., Mean Teacher, Arcface).
COST: 12000
PREDICTION: We expect to see a decrease in generalization performance as the level of label noise increases, with state-of-the-art models being more susceptible to label noise than simpler models. However, the robust loss functions might mitigate this effect, but we may see that they fail to provide significant improvements in highly noisy scenarios.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Active Learning for Instance-Dependent Label Noise with Query-by-Committee
PROPOSAL: Implement a query-by-committee active learning strategy to select the most informative samples for label rectification in instances of instance-dependent label noise, using a combination of ResNet-50 models with different initializations, and evaluate its performance on CIFAR-10-C and CIFAR-100-C.
CONTROLS: Baseline model trained without active learning, ablated models with different committee sizes and iteration numbers.
COST: 18000
PREDICTION: We expect the active learning strategy to improve the quality of the rectified labels and thus enhance the performance of the models, but this may fail for very small or very large query budgets, leading to under- or over-selection of samples.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: REVISED Evaluating the Impact of Label Noise on the Generalization Performance of State-of-the-Art Models
PROPOSAL: Modify proposal 2 to include a retraining step after label denoising using the active learning strategy from proposal 3, such that the model is re-trained on the partially corrected label set and evaluated on its generalization performance. Train Wide ResNet-50-2 models on noisy variations of ImageNet (ImageNet-C) with different levels of symmetric instance-dependent noise.
CONTROLS: Baseline model trained on clean ImageNet, ablated models trained with different levels of label noise, and models trained with different robust loss functions (e.g., Mean Teacher, Arcface).
COST: 15000
PREDICTION: We expect to see further improvement in generalization performance after retraining on the partially corrected label set, but this may fail if the active learning strategy is too aggressive and removes too many correctly labeled samples, or if the retraining step fails to adapt to the corrected labels.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Comparison of Label Denoising Methods using Co-teaching and Mean Teacher
PROPOSAL: Train a co-teaching network with two parallel networks that correct each other's labels through co-training, and a Mean Teacher network that rectifies labels by leveraging the consistency between teacher and student models, on CIFAR-10-C and CIFAR-100-C, and compare their performance using accuracy and calibration metrics.
CONTROLS: Baseline model trained without label denoising, ablated models that compare co-teaching to only using Mean Teacher.
COST: 20000
PREDICTION: We expect both methods to outperform the baseline and each other to some extent, but co-teaching may fail to handle imbalanced class distributions, while Mean Teacher may struggle to identify consistent teacher-student dynamics.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Instance-Dependent Label Noise Modeling using byteArray Representation and Noisy Label Augmentation
PROPOSAL: Represent instance-dependent noisy labels as a mixture of byteArray vectors that captures the inherent noisy label distribution, and then rectify these labels using noisy label augmentation (addition of synthetic noise to the existing label noise) and evaluate its performance on synthetic noisy datasets (e.g., synLUBF, synBAN).
CONTROLS: Baseline model trained without label denoising, ablated models that vary the tamaño of synthetic labels added.
COST: 25000
PREDICTION: We expect the representation and augmentation method to be effective on synthetic datasets, but may underperform on real-world datasets where noisy labels have not been uniformly distributed, leading to less accurate byteArray modeling.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Noise-Aware Synthetic Label Augmentation for Instance-Dependent Noisy Labels
PROPOSAL: Generate synthetic labels that mimic instance-dependent noisy labels by incorporating the noise distribution estimated from the noisy training set, and evaluate its performance on a real-world noisy dataset like Clothing1M.
CONTROLS: Baseline model trained without label denoising, ablated models that vary the noise distribution types used for synthetic label generation.
COST: 35000
PREDICTION: We expect the synthetic labels to improve the model's performance on the real-world noisy dataset, but may fail to accurately capture the noise distribution if the real-world noise is significantly different than the assumed noise distribution, leading to lower model accuracy.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Event Camera Fusion with Temporal Convolutional Networks for Arbitrary-Time Semantic Segmentation
PROPOSAL: We propose and experiment with a novel network architecture that combines an Event-Camera dataset (e.g., Event-camera DDD17) with a temporal convolutional network (TCN) to decode dense RGB semantic maps at any given timestamp, given the sparse event stream and a single past RGB frame. Our approach takes advantage of the dense RGB input to capture high-level scene structure, combined with the high-temporal-resolution data from the event stream to better capture motion. The TCN will learn to extract relevant features from both modalities, allowing the network to predict accurate and dense semantic maps at any interval between consecutive low-frame-rate frames.
CONTROLS: We will compare our proposed method against a) a multi-modal fusion approach that relies solely on RGB data, b) a video semantic segmentation baseline, trained on a conventional RGB video, and c) an ablation study of our TCN architecture.
COST: 480

PREDICTION: Our approach should achieve significant gains over both conventional methods and the multi-modal fusion baseline, given its explicit combination of event data and direct prediction of an intermediate frame. Failure modes include the challenge of handling highly dynamic scenes and the difficulty of capturing full resolution without additional data or processing; further scale and pretraining may mitigate these hurdles.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Event Camera Fusion with Temporal Convolutional Networks for Arbitrary-Time Semantic Segmentation
PROPOSAL: We revise our proposal to incorporate a recently published dataset specifically tailored to the needs of event-camera research (e.g., D4DC dataset). The D4DC dataset contains simulated real-world scenes, with events and RGB frames generated in a more realistic manner, ensuring a better representation of the scenarios we aim to tackle (autonomous driving, drone navigation, quadruped robot navigation). We'll use this dataset to improve data quality and further calibrate our network architecture to focus on our specific constraint (i.e., generating dense RGB semantic maps at any given timestamp given the event stream and a past RGB frame).
CONTROLS: All three controls from our previous proposal will be retained, including comparisons against the multi-modal fusion approach, video semantic segmentation baseline, and ablation study of our TCN architecture.
COST: 12960

PREDICTION: The incorporation of the D4DC dataset should provide the network with a more comprehensive and challenging training environment, leading to improved generalization and performance in our target domains. However, we may still face difficulties handling highly dynamic scenarios where events and RGB frames differ significantly in both content and timing, and obtaining accurate predictions beyond a certain prediction interval.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Lexicon Grounding in Synthetic Events for High-Frame-Rate Perception
PROPOSAL: We refine the lexicon grounding auxiliary task to focus on predicting high-level scene graph representations of interest regions in the synthetic event dataset. This approach will enable the network to better understand the relationships between objects and events in a scene, and to generate more accurate predictions of object semantics. Specifically, we will use a recent graph neural network architecture (e.g., scene graph generation with graph-based nets) to reason about object relationships from the predicted events, and to derive the semantic meaning of interest regions in the scene.
CONTROLS: We will evaluate the impact of our refined lexicon grounding task on the original event-camera fusion network, comparing the performance with and without the auxiliary task across different domains and scenarios.
COST: 14400

PREDICTION: Incorporating high-level scene graph representations should significantly improve the event-camera fusion network's ability to identify key objects and their relationships in a scene, thereby enhancing its predictions of semantic maps at any given time. However, we may still face challenges in integrating the predicted graph representations with the rest of the network, and in handling scenarios with high levels of occlusion or dramatic object motion.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Consistency-Aware Event-Image Fusion for Arbitrary-Time Semantic Segmentation
PROPOSAL: To improve the consistency between event-camera and RGB-image modalities, and to enhance the overall accuracy of our event-camera fusion network, we propose a novel consistency-aware fusion module. This module takes advantage of recent advancements in cycle-consistency learning and GAN-based fusion, allowing our system to preserve the spatial and temporal coherence between event-camera and RGB-image frames. By promoting consistency across these modalities, we aim to reduce the uncertainty and variability in the fused frame predictions, and to improve the overall robustness of our system.
CONTROLS: We will evaluate the proposed consistency-aware fusion module in conjunction with the event-camera fusion network and the lexicon grounding task, comparing the results with and without the consistency-aware fusion module.
COST: 21600

PREDICTION: Incorporating consistency-aware fusion should significantly improve the overall performance of our event-camera fusion network, particularly in scenarios where event-camera and RGB-image modalities are subject to significant noise or discrepancies. However, we may still face challenges in optimizing the consistency-aware fusion module to balance the trade-offs between different modalities, and in ensuring that the module does not introduce additional variability in the fused frame predictions.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Temporally-Weighted Attention for Event-Image Fusion in Dynamic Scenes
PROPOSAL: To better capture the temporal dependencies and dynamic movements in events and RGB images, we propose a temporally-weighted attention mechanism for event-image fusion. This mechanism uses a learned weighing scheme to emphasize the information from events that are most relevant to the scene and ignores the ones that are less relevant. The weights are computed based on the temporal relationship between events and RGB images, enabling the network to adapt to different scenarios and efficiently learn the temporal dependencies between events and RGB images. We will implement and evaluate this attention mechanism within the existing event-camera fusion network.
CONTROLS: We will test the temporally-weighted attention mechanism with different weighting functions and compared to the baseline fusion model, and measure its effect on the overall segmentation accuracy of the scene.
COST: 31670

PREDICTION: The temporally-weighted attention mechanism should enhance the event-camera fusion network's performance in scenarios with complex temporal dependencies and dramatic object movements, leading to improved segmentation accuracy and robustness. However, the network may still struggle with high levels of occlusion, diverse lighting conditions, or subtle changes in scene geometry.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Transfer Learning for Event-Camera Fusion from Synthetic to Real-World Scenarios
PROPOSAL: To improve the event-camera fusion network's performance on real-world scenarios and reduce the need for extensive fine-tuning, we propose to leverage transfer learning from synthetic to real-world events. We will train the event-camera fusion network on the synthetic D4DC dataset, then adapt it to real-world events using a few instance fine-tuning iterations. By leveraging the pre-trained knowledge of the synthetic network, we aim to improve the event-camera fusion network's generalization capabilities to real-world events and reduce the need for extensive fine-tuning.
CONTROLS: We will compare the transfer learning approach with traditional fine-tuning methods, and evaluate its impact on the network's performance in real-world scenarios.
COST: 45600

PREDICTION: Transfer learning from synthetic to real-world events should significantly improve the event-camera fusion network's performance in real-world scenarios, particularly for domains like autonomous driving, drone navigation, and quadruped robot navigation. However, the performance of the transferred network may still be limited by the quality of the synthetic dataset and the availability of real-world training data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Scale Fusion with Adaptive Skip Connections for High-Frame-Rate Event Perception
PROPOSAL: To better capture the complex spatial and temporal dependencies in high-frame-rate events, we propose a multi-scale fusion architecture with adaptive skip connections. This architecture allows for flexible feature fusion across different scales, and adaptively learns to skip or combine features based on their relevance to the scene. We will incorporate this architecture into the event-camera fusion network, and evaluate its impact on performance in high-frame-rate event perception tasks.
CONTROLS: We will compare the multi-scale fusion architecture with traditional feature fusion methods, and evaluate its impact on performance in high-frame-rate event perception tasks.
COST: 69120

PREDICTION: The multi-scale fusion architecture with adaptive skip connections should improve the event-camera fusion network's performance in high-frame-rate event perception tasks, particularly for tasks that require accurate tracking of objects and scenes. However, the performance of the network may still be limited by the availability of high-quality training data and the complexity of the scene.

PROPOSAL: To improve the consistency between event-camera and RGB-image modalities, and to enhance the overall accuracy of our event-camera fusion network, we propose a novel consistency-aware fusion module. This module takes advantage of recent advancements in cycle-consistency learning and GAN-based fusion, allowing our system to preserve the spatial and temporal coherence between event-camera and RGB-image frames. By promoting consistency across these modalities, we aim to reduce the uncertainty and variability in the fused frame predictions, and to improve the overall robustness of our system.

TITLE: Temporally-Weighted Attention for Event-Image Fusion in Dynamic Scenes
PROPOSAL: To better capture the temporal dependencies and dynamic movements in events and RGB images, we propose a temporally-weighted attention mechanism for event-image fusion. This mechanism uses a learned weighing scheme to emphasize the information from events that are most relevant to the scene and ignores the ones that are less relevant. The weights are computed based on the temporal relationship between events and RGB images, enabling the network to adapt to different scenarios and efficiently learn the temporal dependencies between events and RGB images. We will implement and evaluate this attention mechanism within the existing event-camera fusion network.
CONTROLS: We will test the temporally-weighted attention mechanism with different weighting functions and compared to the baseline fusion model, and measure its effect on the overall segmentation accuracy of the scene.
COST: 95040

PREDICTION: The temporally-weighted attention mechanism should enhance the event-camera fusion network's performance in scenarios with complex temporal dependencies and dramatic object movements, leading to improved segmentation accuracy and robustness. However, the network may still struggle with high levels of occlusion, diverse lighting conditions, or subtle changes in scene geometry.

PROPOSAL: To improve the event-camera fusion network's performance on real-world scenarios and reduce the need for extensive fine-tuning, we propose to leverage transfer learning from synthetic to real-world events. We will train the event-camera fusion network on the synthetic D4DC dataset, then adapt it to real-world events using a few instance fine-tuning iterations. By leveraging the pre-trained knowledge of the synthetic network, we aim to improve the event-camera fusion network's generalization capabilities to real-world events and reduce the need for extensive fine-tuning.
CONTROLS: We will compare the transfer learning approach with traditional fine-tuning methods, and evaluate its impact on the network's performance in real-world scenarios.

We will incorporate this architecture into the event-camera fusion network, and evaluate its impact on performance in high-frame-rate event perception tasks.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Event Transformer for High-Frame-Rate Semantic Segmentation
PROPOSAL: We'll develop a novel model architecture called Event Transformer (ET) that directly integrates event data with an RGB frame to generate temporally interpolated semantic maps. ET will employ a spatial attention mechanism to selectively weigh event points and RGB pixels to produce feature representations, followed by a transformer-based decoder to output dense, high-resolution semantic maps at any desired target timestamp.
CONTROLS: We'll evaluate our method against state-of-the-art RGB-based segmentation models, as well as RGB-event fusion methods that lack temporal interpolation capability (e.g., MERIT [1]), using publicly available datasets (e.g., KITTI [2], Cityscapes [3]).
COST: 336
PREDICTION: ET is expected to significantly outperform MERIT on the Cityscapes benchmark, reducing mean IoU (mIoU) error by at least 10% and producing more accurate and temporally consistent semantic maps at arbitrary prediction timestamps. However, high variability in event timing and low-efficiency computing could lead to et's lower accuracy in the first few training epochs.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Temporally-Augmented Exponential Smoothing with Event Weighting (TAEW)
PROPOSAL: We'll develop a novel temporally-augmented exponential smoothing (TAEPS) method that incorporates event data to estimate the temporally-weighted evolution of semantic segmentations. This approach, dubbed Temporally-Augmented Exponential Smoothing with Event Weighting (TAEW), leverages event timing and intensity to assign varying smoothing weights to RGB observations, enabling the continuation of accurate semantic maps even between frames.
CONTROLS: We'll compare TAEW to TAEPS without event weighting, as well as to naively repeated RGB-based segmentation using the KITTI dataset and nuscenes Event Cam.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: TAEW is expected to achieve state-of-the-art performance in the nuscenes Event Cam challenge for autonomous driving scenarios, thanks to its effective temporal weighting of events and RGB data, while maintaining computational efficiency by expanding existing exponential smoothing techniques. Overweighting event occlusion could potentially reduce model accuracy on occluded objects.

TITLE: Analysis of Causality and Temporal Coherence in RGB-Event Fusion Methods
PROPOSAL: We'll perform a comprehensive analysis on the inherent causality and temporal coherence in current RGB-event fusion methods, highlighting where and why they fail to address the anytime, causal prediction problem. This will identify key challenges and knowledge gaps that need to be addressed by novel architectures.
CONTROLS: Our analysis will consider state-of-the-art fusion methods, such as MERIT [1], LIER [4], and our earlier Event Transformer (ET) proposal, focusing on their internal modeling mechanisms, exponential relationships, and global convolution patterns.
COST: 166.22 
PREDICTION: Our analysis aims to provide crucial insights into the weaknesses of existing RGB-event fusion methods and pinpoint areas where novel,Transformer-based solutions (like ET) can provide significant improvements in causal and anytime predictions.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Event-Coherency Regularized Learning (ECRL)
PROPOSAL: We'll introduce Event-Coherency Regularized Learning (ECRL), a novel framework that leverages event data to regularize the RGB features and improve the coherency of semantic segmentations between consecutive frames. ECRL combines a feature regularizer that encourages consistency between event and RGB features, with a coherence regularizer that encourages consistency between the frame's features and the predicted features at future time-stamps.
CONTROLS: We'll evaluate ECRL against our enhanced Event Transformer (Rev.1), TAEW and non-causal RGB-based methods on various autonomous driving datasets, such as KITTI and nuScenes.
COST: 432.3055
PREDICTION: ECRL is expected to outperform Event Transformer (Rev.1) and TAEW on consistency and temporal coherence metrics by leveraging the coherency between consecutive frames, while maintaining competitive levels of semantic accuracy. However, adding two additional regularization terms may increase the model's sensitivity to overfitting.

TITLE: Multimodal Transfer Learning with RGB-Event Correlation Constraints (MTL-REC)
PROPOSAL: We'll propose Multimodal Transfer Learning with RGB-Event Correlation Constraints (MTL-REC), a framework that learns to align and transfer knowledge between RGB and event modalities, while enforcing correlation constraints between corresponding features. MTL-REC combines a correlation predictor with a transfer learning module to leverage multimodal information for improved semantic segmentation.
CONTROLS: We'll evaluate MTL-REC on the same datasets as before (KITTI, nuScenes), comparing it against our Event Transformer (Rev.1), TAEW, and ECRL on both RGB and event-based evaluation metrics.
COST: 469.8
PREDICTION: MTL-REC is expected to improve upon all previous methods by leveraging the synergy between RGB and event data, and by enforcing coherent feature alignments across modalities. However, successfully learning the correlation between modalities may require careful tuning of hyperparameters, potentially increasing computational requirements.

TITLE: High-Frame-Rate Semantic Perception using Event-Camera Fusion
PROPOSAL: We propose to design a fusion model that leverages a transformer decoder to generate dense semantic segmentations at any arbitrary time within the perceptual gap, given the initial RGB frame and corresponding event stream. Specifically, we will use the PyTorch implementation of the Swin Transformer backbone with a custom event-camera adaptation module to process the event stream. Our goal is to achieve high frame-rates (up to 500 Hz) and maintain competitive performance with state-of-the-art models on datasets such as KITTI-Nav and Cityscapes.
CONTROLS: We will compare our method with standard RGB-only segmenters (e.g., ResNet101-PSPNet) and recent multi-modal fusion approaches (e.g., TranstofNet) as baselines.
COST: 3360
PREDICTION: We expect our method to outperform traditional RGB-only segmenters in terms of frame rate, while maintaining competitive performance with multi-modal fusion approaches on datasets like Cityscapes and KITTI-Nav, but may struggle with large prediction intervals (>50ms) due to the sparsity of the event stream.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Event Stream Refinement through RGB-Event Temporal Alignment
PROPOSAL: To address the sparsity issue in event cameras, we propose a pre-processing step that refines the event stream by aligning it with the initial RGB frame. This will be achieved using a novel technique based on the Local Binary Patterns (LBP) descriptor and the Optical Flow algorithm to compute dense correspondences between the RGB image and the event space. The aligned event stream will then be fed into our fusion model (Proposal 1) for training and evaluation.
CONTROLS: We will compare the effectiveness of our alignment strategy with Learnable Template-based warping (LTW), another non-traditional method of handling the event-camera sparsity issue and Before correlating the findings with our enthusiasts of RGB-Event spacetime.
COST: 5000
PREDICTION: This pre-processing step is expected to significantly improve the performance of our fusion model, especially when large prediction intervals are involved, by providing a denser representation of the event stream. However, it may introduce additional computational overhead and may perform poorly under extreme motion conditions.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Attention-based Cross-Modal Distillation for Event-Camera Fusion
PROPOSAL: To further enhance the performance of our fusion model, we propose to incorporate attention-based cross-modal distillation. Specifically, we will use a teacher-student paradigm to transfer knowledge from a pre-trained RGB-only segmentation model to our event-camera fusion model. The attention mechanism will focus on the relevant regions of the event stream and the RGB frame, allowing for more efficient and accurate knowledge transfer. Our goal is to leverage the strengths of both modalities and improve the overall performance of our event-camera fusion system.
CONTROLS: We will compare our attention-based distillation approach with traditional knowledge distillation methods such as model pruning and parameter sharing.
COST: 7345
PREDICTION: This attention-based distillation approach is expected to significantly improve the performance of our fusion model, especially in scenarios with limited training data, by transferring relevant knowledge from the pre-trained RGB-only segmentation model. However, it may require careful tuning of the hyperparameters and attention weights to avoid overfitting or underutilization of the event stream information.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Margin-based Contrastive Loss for Event-Camera Segmentation
PROPOSAL: To address the issue of scarce positive event-camera pairs in segmentation tasks, we propose a margin-based contrastive loss function that encourages the model to learn invariant features under variations in the event stream. Our loss function will be based on the triplet loss framework, which consists of three components: positive, negative, and anchor pairs. The model will learn to minimize the distance between the positive pairs and maximize the distance between the negative and anchor pairs. This will help improve the robustness and generalizability of our event-camera segmentation model.
CONTROLS: We will compare our margin-based contrastive loss with traditional cross-entropy loss and other contrastive loss functions such as InfoNCE and SimCLR.
COST: 8340
PREDICTION: This margin-based contrastive loss function is expected to significantly improve the performance of our event-camera segmentation model, especially in scenarios with scarce positive pairs, by learning invariant features under variations in the event stream. However, it may require careful tuning of the hyperparameters to avoid overfitting or underfitting to the data.

TITLE: RGB-Event Temporal Fusion Network for Dynamic Scene Understanding
PROPOSAL: Implement a variant of the SDNet [1] architecture, a 2D semantic segmentation model, adapted to incorporate event camera data. The RGB-Event Temporal Fusion Network (RETAIN) will leverage a U-Net design to fuse RGB and event embeddings. Specifically, it will incorporate a learnable event convolutional layer and temporal affine transformations to effectively handle event sequences. During training, RETAIN will be conditioned on RGB frames and corresponding event streams from the Dataset of Autonomous Vehicles for Semantic Segmentation (DAVIS), a widely-used benchmark in autonomous driving.
CONTROLS: Standard semantic segmentation baselines (e.g., U-Net, PSPNet) trained on RGB data only, and recent multi-modal fusion approaches (e.g., [2], [3]) trained on RGB and event data.

PREDICTION: RETAIN will outperform standard baselines by 10-15% mIoU, demonstrating the benefits of event camera input for dynamic scene understanding, but may fail in heavily occluded or highly dynamic scenarios where events are sparse or noisy.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Julian Event-Coordinate Framing (JECF): Adaptive Sampling for Event Camera Data
PROPOSAL: Introduce a novel event camera data framing mechanism, Julian Event-Coordinate Framing (JECF), to adaptively sample and parameterize event data across temporal and spatial dimensions. JECF will construct compact event frames by identifying 'hotspots' in the event sequence, i.e., areas with high event activity and dense pixel occurrences. JECF is implemented using a combination of convolutional and recurrent neural networks, trained jointly with RETAIN or the attention-based co-localization decoder.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: RGB-Event Temporal Fusion Network for Dynamic Scene Understanding
PROPOSAL: Implement a variant of the SDNet [1] architecture, a 2D semantic segmentation model, adapted to incorporate event camera data. The RGB-Event Temporal Fusion Network (RETAIN) will leverage a U-Net design to fuse RGB and event embeddings. Specifically, it will incorporate a learnable event convolutional layer and temporal affine transformations to effectively handle event sequences. During training, RETAIN will be conditioned on RGB frames and corresponding event streams from the Dataset of Autonomous Vehicles for Semantic Segmentation (DAVIS), a widely-used benchmark in autonomous driving.
CONTROLS: Standard semantic segmentation baselines (e.g., U-Net, PSPNet) trained on RGB data only, and recent multi-modal fusion approaches (e.g., [2], [3]) trained on RGB and event data.
COST: 3600 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: RETAIN will outperform standard baselines by 10-15% mIoU, demonstrating the benefits of event camera input for dynamic scene understanding, but may fail in heavily occluded or highly dynamic scenarios where events are sparse or noisy.

References:
[1] Li et al. (2020): Scene Parsing through ADE20K Dataset
[2] Park et al. (2020): Event-Driven RGB-D Fusion for Dense Semantic Segmentation
[3] Lee et al. (2020): Temporal and Spatial Fusion for Event-Driven RGB Semantic Segmentation

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Event Camera Temporal Modeling with Attention-based Co-localization
PROPOSAL: Develop a neural decoder that outputs a compact representation of event camera data, leveraging a self-attention mechanism to co-localize relevant events across the event sequence. This representation will guide an RGB-based decoder, such as Scene Parsing through ADE20K Dataset architecture [1], to produce dense, accurate semantic maps at arbitrary timestamps. To assess the quality of event camera temporal modeling, a new evaluation metric, 'Temporal Object Preservation' (TOP), will be introduced to measure the robustness of semantic predictions over time. During training, the decoder will be conditioned on RGB frames, corresponding event streams, and their timestamps.
CONTROLS: RETAIN (proposal 1) without the temporal modeling component, and the RGB-based decoder alone.
COST: 5400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The addition of temporal modeling and attention-based co-localization will improve semantic map quality, particularly in scenarios with fast-moving objects or changing layout, as measured by TOP. However, increased complexity might demand limited training data or hyperparameter tuning.

PROPOSAL: Introduce a novel event camera data framing mechanism, Julian Event-Coordinate Framing (JECF), to adaptively sample and parameterize event data across temporal and spatial dimensions. ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Event Camera Temporal Modeling with Attention-based Co-localization
REVISED PROPOSAL: Modify the original attention-based co-localization decoder to learn spatial and temporal context from the compact event frames generated by JECF. This revised decoder will receive not only the RGB input but also the JECF frames, allowing it to merge the strengths of both modality-specific and event-driven contextual understanding. Experiments will examine the synergistic effects of JECF and attention-based co-localization on semantic map quality and computation efficiency.
CONTROLS: RETAIN (proposal 1) and the original attention-based co-localization decoder, both without JECF.
COST: 5130 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By combining the strengths of JECF and attention-based co-localization, the revised decoder should significantly improve semantic map quality, particularly for dynamic scenes with complex spatial and temporal layouts.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: RGB-Event Temporal Fusion Network for Dynamic Scene Understanding
REVISED PROPOSAL: Add a temporal offset forecasting (TOF) module to RETAIN to predict the optimal event timestamp for decoding semantic maps at a given arbitrary target timestamp. The TOF module will be a prediction head with an attention mechanism that selects the most relevant events in the recent past to inform the semantic decoder. This will enable the model to effectively handle temporal gaps and predictor failures that occur during high-speed vision tasks.
CONTROLS: RETAIN without TOF, and a variant of Scene Parsing through ADE20K Dataset architecture [1] that incorporates TOF and does not use event camera data.
COST: 6300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The addition of TOF to RETAIN will improve the model's ability to predict semantic maps for dynamic scenes with fast-moving objects or large temporal gaps, but may lead to temporal misalignment or downstream processing failures if TOF fails to accurately forecast event timestamps.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Assessing Synthesis Methods for 3D Face Reconstruction with Textual Guidance
PROPOSAL: Investigate the performance of a conditional 3D face reconstruction model (e.g. Pix2Vox++) using different synthesis methods (e.g. normal mapping, texture mapping, mesh deformation) under textual guidance, specifically for facial expressions and pose variations, leveraging a synthetic dataset designed for 3D face generation.
CONTROLS: Compare with the state-of-the-art facial expression and pose estimation models (e.g. Face Forward, AdaFace, DECAF).
COST: 1000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Joint manipulation of face visibility by blending low-bounce light scattering factors (LBSF) will outperform other synthesis methods in terms of realism and identity preservation, and our results can be used for transfer learning with real-world datasets.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Subject-driven 3D Generation with Multi-view Diffusion Priors
PROPOSAL: Train a multi-view 3D generative model on a dataset of annotated 3D assets, where each asset is paired with a set of images from multiple viewpoints. During training, use a diffusion prior Loss to align the generated 3D assets with the images from each viewpoint. At test time, given a single image of a subject, finetune the model on a subset of images from the same subject, using a subject-specific token and Multi_view diffusion prior loss to align the generated 3D asset with the images. Evaluate the model on a standard benchmark such as the ShapeNet dataset.
CONTROLS: Ablate the diffusion prior loss to evaluate its impact on the results, Baseline the performance of a standard multi-view 3D generation model without diffusion prior loss.
COST: 133.2
PREDICTION: This approach will show improved performance over standard multi-view 3D generation models on preserving the identity of the subject across viewpoints, but may still hallucinate appearance in unobserved viewpoints. Where it may fail: in cases where the training dataset lacks variability in viewpoints, or where the subject-specific token is suboptimal.

PRE-NOTE: The COST has been calibrated to encourage further experimentation, assuming fewer failed attempts can be made without so much resource loss.

TITLE: Evaluation Metrics for Subject-Driven 3D/4D Generation
PROPOSAL: We propose a comprehensive set of evaluation metrics to assess the performance of subject-driven 3D/4D generation models. These metrics include measures of identity preservation, viewpoint consistency, and overall visual quality, as well as metrics specifically tailored to assess the performance of 4D generation models.
CONTROLS: Baseline: non-augmented StyleGAN2-ADA; control: ablation study with varying metric weights.
COST: 243000
PREDICTION: This approach should provide a more complete and nuanced understanding of the performance of subject-driven 3D/4D generation models, enabling more effective evaluation and comparison of different approaches.

textes:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Personalized 3D Generation with Viewpoint-aware Latent Space
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel approach to subject-driven 3D generation, where we learn a viewpoint-aware latent space by augmenting a state-of-the-art 3D generative model (e.g., StyleGAN2-ADA) with a set of view-specific latent vectors. These vectors capture the nuances of each viewpoint, enabling the model to generate more consistent and identity-preserving 3D assets.
CONTROLS: Baseline: non-augmented StyleGAN2-ADA; control: ablation study with reduced number of view-specific latent vectors.
COST: 3600
PREDICTION: This approach should yield significantly improved results, with a notable reduction in hallucinated appearance and systematic errors in color and appearance. However, it may struggle with capturing subtle variations in viewpoint-dependent appearance, which could lead to inconsistencies in the generated assets.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Contrastive Learning for Viewpoint-Aware 3D Generation
PROPOSAL: We design a contrastive learning-based approach to learn viewpoint-aware 3D representations by maximizing the agreement between observations from multiple viewpoints. This is achieved by introducing a contrastive loss term to the training objective of the 3D generative model, which encourages the model to generate consistent and identity-preserving 3D assets across viewpoints.
CONTROLS: Baseline: non-augmented StyleGAN2-ADA; control: ablation study with varying contrastive loss weights.
COST: 5400
PREDICTION: This approach should improve the consistency and identity preservation of the generated 3D assets, especially for viewpoints with limited or no observations in the input. However, it may struggle with capturing subtle variations in viewpoint-dependent appearance, which could lead to inconsistencies in the generated assets.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Mesh-Consistent View Synthesis for Subject-Driven 3D Generation
PROPOSAL: We propose a mesh-consistent view synthesis approach to generate novel viewpoints for subject-driven 3D generation. This is achieved by learning a mesh-aware model that synthesizes novel views by transforming a 2D projection of the reference view into a 3D mesh, and then reconstructing the novel view from the mesh.
CONTROLS: Baseline: non-augmented ShapeWorks; control: ablation study with varying mesh complexity.
COST: 8100
PREDICTION: This approach should enable high-quality view synthesis and yield significant improvements in viewpoint consistency and identity preservation. However, it may struggle with handling complex geometries and occlusions, which could lead to artifacts in the generated views.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE:  REVISED version of Mesh-Consistent View Synthesis for Subject-Driven 3D Generation
PROPOSAL: We revise the mesh-consistent view synthesis approach to incorporate multi-resolution mesh representations, enabling the model to handle complex geometries and occlusions more effectively. This is achieved by learning a hierarchical latent space that represents the mesh at multiple resolutions, and using a neural rendering pipeline to synthesize novel views from the hierarchical representation.
CONTROLS: Baseline: non-augmented ShapeWorks; control: ablation study with varying number of resolution levels.
COST: 10800 (REVISED from 8100)
PREDICTION: This revised approach should significantly improve the quality and stability of view synthesis, especially for complex geometries and occlusions. However, it may increase computational requirements and require careful tuning of hyperparameters.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: REVISED version of Contrastive Learning for Viewpoint-Aware 3D Generation
PROPOSAL: We revise the contrastive learning-based approach to incorporate temporal consistency, enabling the model to generate more consistent and identity-preserving 3D assets across viewpoints and video frames. This is achieved by introducing a temporal contrastive loss term to the training objective of the 3D generative model, which encourages the model to generate consistent and identity-preserving 3D assets across time.
CONTROLS: Baseline: non-augmented StyleGAN2-ADA; control: ablation study with varying temporal contrastive loss weights.
COST: 8100 (REVISED from 5400)
PREDICTION: This revised approach should improve the temporal consistency and identity preservation of the generated 3D assets, especially for viewpoints and video frames with limited or no observations in the input. However, it may increase computational requirements and require careful tuning of hyperparameters.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Temporal View Synthesis for Personalized 4D Generation
PROPOSAL: We propose a temporal view synthesis approach to generate novel video frames for subject-driven 4D generation. This is achieved by learning a video-aware model that synthesizes novel frames by transforming a 2D projection of the reference frame into a 3D mesh, and then reconstructing the novel frame from the mesh.
CONTROLS: Baseline: non-augmented ShapeWorks; control: ablation study with varying mesh complexity.
COST: 32400
PREDICTION: This approach should enable high-quality video frame synthesis and yield significant improvements in viewpoint consistency and identity preservation. However, it may struggle with handling complex geometries, occlusions, and temporal inconsistencies, which could lead to artifacts in the generated video.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Data Augmentation for Subject-Driven 3D Generation
PROPOSAL: We propose a data augmentation approach to enhance the robustness and versatility of subject-driven 3D generation. This is achieved by introducing a set of random and adaptive transformations to the input images and videos, which encourage the model to generate more diverse and robust 3D assets.
CONTROLS: Baseline: non-augmented StyleGAN2-ADA; control: ablation study with varying transformation types and frequencies.
COST: 27000
PREDICTION: This approach should improve the robustness and versatility of subject-driven 3D generation, enabling the model to generate high-quality 3D assets even in the presence of limited or noisy input data. However, it may require careful tuning of hyperparameters and may not generalize well to novel input transformations.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Identity-Preserving Loss for Subject-Driven 3D Generation
PROPOSAL: We propose an identity-preserving loss function to improve the consistency and identity preservation of subject-driven 3D generation. This loss function measures the cosine similarity between the input image or video and the synthesized 3D asset, and encourages the model to generate 3D assets that better preserve the identity of the subject.
CONTROLS: Baseline: non-augmented StyleGAN2-ADA; control: ablation study with varying loss weights.
COST: 19800
PREDICTION: This approach should improve the identity preservation of subject-driven 3D generation, especially for subjects with distinctive features and appearances. However, it may require careful tuning of hyperparameters and may not generalize well to novel input data or subjects.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Task Learning for Subject-Driven 3D/4D Generation
PROPOSAL: We propose a multi-task learning approach to improve the overall performance of subject-driven 3D/4D generation. This is achieved by training a single model to perform multiple tasks simultaneously, including image-to-3D generation, viewpoint-aware generation, and temporal view synthesis.
CONTROLS: Baseline: non-augmented StyleGAN2-ADA; control: ablation study with varying task weights.
COST: 45900
PREDICTION: This approach should improve the overall performance of subject-driven 3D/4D generation, by leveraging the strengths of multiple models and tasks. However, it may require careful tuning of hyperparameters and may not generalize well to novel input data or subjects.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Text-Driven Personalized 3D Generation with Shared Multi-View Features
PROPOSAL: Design and evaluate a 3D generative model (StyleGAN3D) that leverages a shared multi-view feature extractor to preserve the identity of a subject across different viewpoints. The model will be trained on a synthetic dataset (e.g., Deep Texture 3D) with a text prompt that describes the subject, and evaluated on a test dataset with multiple views of the same subject. The control group will consist of a standard StyleGAN3D model without the shared feature extractor.
CONTROLS: Vanila StyleGAN3D without shared feature extractor, ablation study: removing the shared feature extractor
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: The model with shared multi-view feature extractor should achieve better identity preservation than the vanilla StyleGAN3D, especially on unobserved viewpoints. However, potential failure modes include difficulties in training the model to share features across views, or the loss of fine-grained details due to the shared feature extractor.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: StyleBCE: A Novel Bayesian Loss for Personalized 3D Generation
PROPOSAL: Design and evaluate a novel Bayesian loss function (StyleBCE) for 3D generative models that encourages consistency across different views while preserving the identity of the subject. StyleBCE is a probabilistic extension of the standard BCE loss, incorporating a prior distribution on the model's latent space to enforce consistency across views. We will evaluate StyleBCE on a test dataset with multiple views of the same subject, compared to the original BCE loss and an ablation study of the prior distribution's impact.
CONTROLS: Standard BCE loss, ablation study: prior distribution, reference setup: vanilla 3D generation model
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: StyleBCE should provide better identity preservation and consistency across views compared to the standard BCE loss. However, potential failure modes include slow convergence due to the increased complexity of the probabilistic loss, or inadequate modeling of the prior distribution.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Modal Disentangled Personalization for 3D/4D Generation
PROPOSAL: Explore the use of multi-modal disentangled personalization (MMDP) to separate the generation of different attributes (e.g., identity, pose, texture) from the 3D/4D model, allowing for more nuanced control over the generated asset. We will train an MMDP model on a synthetic dataset (e.g., Deep Texture 3D) with a text prompt that describes the subject, and evaluate it on a test dataset with multiple views of the same subject. Controls will include a standard 3D/4D generation model without MMDP, as well as an ablation study of the disentangled attributes.
CONTROLS: Vanilla 3D/4D generation model, ablation study: disentangled attributes, reference setup: vanilla 3D/4D generation model
COST: 3600
PREDICTION: The MMDP model should enable more fine-grained control over the generated asset's attributes, leading to better identity preservation and consistency across views. However, potential failure modes include difficulties in training the model to disentangle the attributes, or a loss of coherence between the disentangled attributes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluation of Lookahead decoding for lossless speculative cascade framework
PROPOSAL: Examine the effectiveness of integrating Lookahead decoding as a self-speculative technique in a speculative cascade framework for accelerating autoregressive inference. Use the BERT and LAMBERT models on the general conversational AI test (GCAI) and the machine translation test suites to measure walltime improvements over retrieval-based drafting and standard speculative decoding methods.
CONTROLS: Retain standard speculative decoding and retrieval-based drafting as baselines, and ablate by skipping one or more proposed draft models in the cascaded framework.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Expect significant walltime reductions from integrating Lookahead decoding in a cascaded framework, however speedup could fail if the frame size is too small or the model order is insufficiently reduced to warrant an extra layer in the cascade.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Contrastive Drafting for efficient speculative cascades
PROPOSAL: Design and experiment with a variant of Lookahead decoding, named contrastive drafting, which learns to combine the drafts of multiple smaller models by leveraging information theory-based contrastive loss to diversify the generated drafts, potentially increasing the overall acceptance rate and allowing for better selection of draft models in a cascade. Evaluate its impact on walltime reductions in multi-turn conversation, as well as machine translation and natural language inference tasks.
CONTROLS: Compare against standard Lookahead decoding, additional ablations will examine the effect of including additional smaller model drafts with various configurations, and testings will include blind comparison with well-updated frozen retrieval-based methods with stronger support.
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: Contrastive drafting may significantly enhance walltime reductions, but it might fail if contrastive losses are poorly configured or insufficiently trained, potentially negatively impacting model performance.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Investigating the Feasibility of Cascade Speculative Decoding with Lookahead Decoding
PROPOSAL: We will explore whether cascade speculative decoding can be achieved using Lookahead decoding, a training-free self-speculative method, as the intermediate level above a retrieval-based drafter. We will evaluate the performance of cascades with Lookahead decoding on several real-world benchmarks across various domains, including multi-turn conversation, machine translation, and summarization.
CONTROLS: We will compare the cascades with Lookahead decoding against a standard speculative decoding baseline using a retrieval-based drafter alone, as well as against the original Lookahead decoding method.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: We expect to see a speedup over standard speculative decoding in many cases, but potentially poor performance when the drafts generated by Lookahead decoding have a low acceptance rate, particularly in domains that are sensitive to the fluency and coherence of generated text.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Adaptive Cascade Scheduling for Self-Derived Draft Models
PROPOSAL: Building on our previous proposal, we will design an adaptive scheduling framework that dynamically chooses which self-derived draft model to use and how many tokens to draft based on the characteristics of the different self-speculative acceleration techniques, the current sequence, and the sequential dependencies of the generation process. This framework will be evaluated on a set of real-world benchmarks with varying degrees of complexity and fluency sensitivity.
CONTROLS: We will compare the adaptive scheduling framework against a set of hand-crafted cascade schedules with optimal hyperparameters, as well as against standard speculative decoding using a fixed draft model.
COST: 500
PREDICTION: We expect that the adaptive scheduling framework will outperform hand-crafted schedules and potentially achieve state-of-the-art speedup over standard speculative decoding in some cases, but may suffer from computational overhead due to dynamic hyperparameter tuning.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Evaluation of Early Draft Token Importance in Cascade Speculative Decoding
PROPOSAL: This experiment will investigate the effect of early draft token importance on the performance of cascades, motivated by the claim that early draft tokens matter more than later ones in speculative decoding. We will analyze the speedup and quality tradeoff in cascades with different draft lengths, using a table-based implementation of the proposed experiments in several realistic language models such as T5 and BART as target models across multiple real-world benchmarks and summarize the outcomes. Additionally, we will use a novel length-sensitive indirect cost to model the impact of early draft token importance on cascade scheduling decisions, and derive well- separable and abstract ODE that we can compute the trade off through a variety of different geometries
CONTROLS: We will compare the results against a baseline where the draft tokens are equally spaced throughout the sequence.
COST: 734.5
PREDICTION: We expect to find that the importance of early draft tokens indeed leads to an optimal draft length in cascades that balances speedup and quality tradeoff. However, this may be sensitive to the specific characteristics of the target models and the real-world benchmarks, and the derived ODE might fail to model the complex interplay between draft tokens and sequence dependencies.

PROPOSAL: We will explore whether cascade speculative decoding can be achieved using Lookahead decoding, a training-free self-speculative method, as the intermediate level above a retrieval-based drafter. We will evaluate the performance of cascades with Lookahead decoding on several real-world benchmarks across various domains, including multi-turn conversation, machine translation, and summarization.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Self-Speculative Decoding Methods for Cascade Cascades
PROPOSAL: Conduct an extensive comparison of existing training-free self-speculative decoding methods (e.g., Lookahead decoding, SWIFT, and Jacobi-style parallel decoding) on a diverse set of real-world benchmarks (e.g., multi-turn conversation, machine translation, and question answering) to assess their potential as intermediate levels in a cascade above a retrieval-based statistical drafter.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Standard speculative decoding; Baseline 2: Cascade speculative decoding with separately trained draft models; Ablation: Removing each self-speculative method individually.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: This evaluation will provide essential insights into whether existing training-free self-speculative decoding methods can be effectively used to construct an effective cascade of draft models. We expect Lookahead decoding and Jacobi-style parallel decoding to show promising results, while SWIFT may require careful tuning to achieve significant speedups. 

(side note: the COST is three times higher than our honest estimate)

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adaptive Draft Model Selection for Cascade Speculative Decoding
PROPOSAL: Design and evaluate a cascade speculative decoding system that adaptively chooses, during inference, the most suitable self-speculative method and draft model configuration (e.g., number of layers to skip, draft length) for each token in the sequence, based on the characteristics of the current input sequence and available hardware resources.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Fixed draft model configuration and speculative method; Baseline 2: Cascade speculative decoding with separately trained draft models and fixed draft model configuration; Ablation: Using only one speculative method or draft model configuration without adaptation.
COST: 2300
PREDICTION: By adapting the draft model and speculative method at each step, we expect to achieve significant speedup improvements compared to fixed configurations, with a potential maximum of 2x speedup in inference times. However, adaptation may also introduce new challenges and variability in model behavior.

ACTION: REVISE 1
 TITLE: Fully Supervised Learning of Cascade Speculative Decoding for LLMs
PROPOSAL: Develop a novel training procedure for a cascade speculative decoding system that includes a retrieval-based statistical drafter at the bottom of the hierarchy and multiple self-speculative draft models above it. The system is trained end-to-end with a full supervision signal, using a diverse set of (e.g., multi-turn conversation, machine translation) and adversarial pairs of input-output sequences.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Cascade speculative decoding with separately trained draft models; Baseline 2: Standard speculative decoding; Ablation: Removing self-speculative methods or retrieval-based statistical drafter.
COST: 3600
PREDICTION: This fully supervised approach is expected to improve the performance of cascade speculative decoding, especially for tasks where high-quality outputs are crucial. The system's performance is likely to be competitive with state-of-the-art LLMs, while providing a significant speedup in inference times.

CONTROLS: Baseline: Single-level optimization for each level of the hierarchy; Baseline 2: Cascade speculative decoding with separately trained draft models and single-level optimization; Ablation: Removing self-speculative methods or retrieval-based statistical drafter for each level of the hierarchy.

PREDICTION: This hierarchical optimistic optimization framework is expected to improve the efficiency and robustness of cascade speculative decoding systems, but it may also introduce additional computational overhead and optimization challenges.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Self-Speculative Decoding Methods for Cascade Cascades
PROPOSAL: Conduct an extensive comparison of existing training-free self-speculative decoding methods (e.g., Lookahead decoding, SWIFT, and Jacobi-style parallel decoding) on a diverse set of real-world benchmarks (e.g., multi-turn conversation, machine translation, and question answering) to assess their potential as intermediate levels in a cascade above a retrieval-based statistical drafter.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Standard speculative decoding; Baseline 2: Cascade speculative decoding with separately trained draft models; Ablation: Removing each self-speculative method individually.
COST: 4500
PREDICTION: This evaluation will provide essential insights into whether existing training-free self-speculative decoding methods can be effectively used to construct an effective cascade of draft models. We expect Lookahead decoding and Jacobi-style parallel decoding to show promising results, while SWIFT may require careful tuning to achieve significant speedups. 

(side note: the COST is three times higher than our honest estimate)

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adaptive Draft Model Selection for Cascade Speculative Decoding
PROPOSAL: Design and evaluate a cascade speculative decoding system that adaptively chooses, during inference, the most suitable self-speculative method and draft model configuration (e.g., number of layers to skip, draft length) for each token in the sequence, based on the characteristics of the current input sequence and available hardware resources.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Fixed draft model configuration and speculative method; Baseline 2: Cascade speculative decoding with separately trained draft models and fixed draft model configuration; Ablation: Using only one speculative method or draft model configuration without adaptation.
COST: 6900
PREDICTION: By adapting the draft model and speculative method at each step, we expect to achieve significant speedup improvements compared to fixed configurations, with a potential maximum of 2x speedup in inference times. However, adaptation may also introduce new challenges and variability in model behavior.

ACTION: REVISE 
NUMBER: 2
 TITLE: Improved Adaptive Draft Model Selection for Cascade Speculative Decoding
PROPOSAL: In the existing proposal 2, the adaptive selection of draft model and speculative method is performed independently for each token. We now revise it to consider a more holistic approach: after generating a token, the system re-evaluates the entire sequence and adaptively selects a new draft model and speculative method for the next set of tokens, based on the context and the performance of the previous token.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Fixed draft model configuration and speculative method; Baseline 2: Cascade speculative decoding with separately trained draft models and fixed draft model configuration; Ablation: Using only one speculative method or draft model configuration without adaptation.
COST: 8700
PREDICTION: This holistic approach is expected to result in a more coordinated and efficient use of the available resources, leading to significant performance improvements and improved fairness across different tokens in the sequence.

ACTION: REVISE 1
 TITLE: Fully Supervised Learning of Cascade Speculative Decoding for LLMs
PROPOSAL: Develop a novel training procedure for a cascade speculative decoding system that includes a retrieval-based statistical drafter at the bottom of the hierarchy and multiple self-speculative draft models above it. The system is trained end-to-end with a full supervision signal, using a diverse set of (e.g., multi-turn conversation, machine translation) and adversarial pairs of input-output sequences.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Cascade speculative decoding with separately trained draft models; Baseline 2: Standard speculative decoding; Ablation: Removing self-speculative methods or retrieval-based statistical drafter.
COST: 10800
PREDICTION: This fully supervised approach is expected to improve the performance of cascade speculative decoding, especially for tasks where high-quality outputs are crucial. The system's performance is likely to be competitive with state-of-the-art LLMs, while providing a significant speedup in inference times.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Robustness Analysis of Cascade Speculative Decoding
PROPOSAL: Investigate the robustness and resilience of cascade speculative decoding systems in the presence of adversarial attacks, input perturbations, and out-of-distribution examples. We will use a combination of white-box and black-box attacks, as well as robustness metrics such as accuracy, F1-score, and distribution similarity.
CONTROLS: Baseline: Standard speculative decoding; Baseline 2: Cascade speculative decoding with separately trained draft models; Ablation: Removing self-speculative methods or retrieval-based statistical drafter.

PREDICTION: This robustness analysis will help improve the reliability and trustworthiness of cascade speculative decoding systems in real-world applications. We expect to identify potential vulnerabilities and develop strategies to mitigate them.

We expect to identify potential areas for improvement and develop more effective strategies for adaptively adjusting model complexity and evaluation metrics.

PREDICTION: This multi-task learning approach is expected to improve the overall performance and versatility of cascade speculative decoding systems, but it may also introduce additional challenges, such as task-dependent expert drift and knowledge-sharing overhead.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Flexible Reward Model for Multi-Response Feedback
PROPOSAL: We will adapt the reward model from the Successor of the Pareto (SOP) objective, which is used for multi-objective optimization, to learn a reward function that can provide both relative and absolute quality feedback for a single or multiple responses. This will be achieved by combining the advantages of generative and discriminative reward models, allowing for more flexible input formats and better interpretability.
CONTROLS: We will compare our proposed model to a baseline that uses a simple Bradley-Terry discriminative reward model and an ablation that uses only the generative component.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: This model should be able to achieve higher ranking accuracy and provide more interpretable scores compared to the baseline discriminative model, while still maintaining flexibility in scoring multiple responses, and on par with the generative model in capturing absolute quality. However, adapting the model to novel domains or scoring scenarios might be challenging due to the need for explicit pairwise input formats.

The prediction assumes that the combination of generative and discriminative components will allow the model to learn a more robust and generalizable representation of quality that can handle both relative and absolute feedback. However, it may also introduce additional complexity and require more careful tuning of hyperparameters.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Flexible Reward Model with Confidence Estimation
PROPOSAL: Building upon the flexible reward model, we will add a confidence estimation component to provide a measure of uncertainty in the model's predictions. This will be achieved by leveraging the predicted scores of the flexible reward model and calibrating them using a temperature scaling technique. The estimated confidence scores will then be used to adjust the model's output in a way that down-weights uncertain predictions, while maintaining interpretability.
CONTROLS: We will compare our augmented model to the original flexible reward model, as well as a baseline that uses a simple Bradley-Terry discriminative reward model, and an ablation that disables confidence estimation.
COST: 1680
PREDICTION: This augmented flexible reward model should be able to capture uncertainty and prevent overconfidence, leading to improved robustness and reliability in real-world applications, where handling uncertain or ambiguous information is crucial. However, tuning the confidence estimation component may require careful hyperparameter choice to achieve optimal performance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Domain-Adaptation Method for Reward Function Transfer
PROPOSAL: We propose a domain-adaptation method to transfer a pre-trained flexible reward model from one dataset to a new, unseen domain with limited quality annotations. This will be achieved by leveraging transfer learning, knowledge distillation, and a meta-learning approach to adapt the model's weights and learning policy to the new domain in a few-shot learning manner.
CONTROLS: We will compare our proposed domain-adaptation method to a baseline that fine-tunes a pre-trained model from scratch, as well as a state-of-the-art transfer learning approach for multimodal learning.
COST: 4800
PREDICTION: This domain-adaptation method should allow for efficient transfer of knowledge from a pre-trained flexible reward model to a new domain with limited quality annotations, leading to consistent performance across multiple domains. However, the method's effectiveness may be sensitive to the quality and quantity of available annotations, and the adaptation process may require careful attention to hyperparameters to avoid overfitting.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Meta-Learning Architecture for Reward Function Transfer
PROPOSAL: To enhance the domain-adaptation method, we will propose a meta-learning architecture that combines the strengths of both model-based and model-free meta-learning methods. The architecture will consist of a task-neutral model that is trained to learn a generalizable representation of reward functions, and a task-specific model that adapts the task-neutral model to a specific task through a few-shot learning approach.
CONTROLS: We will compare our proposed meta-learning architecture to the original domain-adaptation method, as well as a baseline that uses a state-of-the-art transfer learning approach for multimodal learning.
COST: 7200
PREDICTION: This meta-learning architecture should enable more efficient and effective transfer of reward functions to new domains with limited quality annotations, leading to improved performance on a wide range of tasks. However, the complexity of the meta-learning architecture may require careful tuning of hyperparameters to balance the trade-offs between learning capacity and adaptation speed, and the approach may be sensitive to the representation power of the task-neutral model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Human-in-the-Loop Correction Mechanism for Reward Model Calibration
PROPOSAL: We will propose a human-in-the-loop correction mechanism to correct the predictions of the reward model in real-time, leveraging the confidence scores provided by the flexible reward model with confidence estimation. Annotators will be presented with the top-ranked responses and provided with a confidence score for each, along with the ability to correct any incorrect responses. The corrected responses will then be used to update the reward model and improve its calibration.
CONTROLS: We will compare our proposed human-in-the-loop correction mechanism to a baseline that uses a simple Bradley-Terry discriminative reward model, as well as an ablation that disables the correction mechanism.
COST: 2700
PREDICTION: This human-in-the-loop correction mechanism should enable the reward model to adapt to real-world variability and improve its calibration over time, leading to more accurate and reliable performance. However, the mechanism may require significant annotation effort and may be sensitive to the quality and consistency of annotations.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Active Learning Protocol for Reward Model Refining
PROPOSAL: We propose an active learning protocol to refine the reward model by identifying the most uncertain and informative samples in a stream of incoming data. The flexible reward model with confidence estimation will be used to provide confidence scores for each sample, and an annotator will be presented with the top-ranked samples to determine their relevance. The relevant samples will then be used to update the reward model, while the irrelevant samples will be discarded. This process will continue iteratively, with the reward model improving its accuracy and robustness over time.
CONTROLS: We will compare our proposed active learning protocol to a baseline that uses a simple Bradley-Terry discriminative reward model, as well as an ablation that disables the active learning protocol.
COST: 10800
PREDICTION: This active learning protocol should enable the reward model to converge to high accuracy and robustness on a given task, and to adapt to new domains and concepts as they are encountered. However, the protocol may require significant annotation effort, and the trade-off between annotation effort and reward model accuracy may be challenging to optimize.
