ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adaptive Configuration via Dynamic Meta-Optimizer
PROPOSAL: We introduce a meta-optimizer that takes as input the current state of the model, the training data, and the desired performance metrics, and outputs a configuration (data augmentation strategy, optimizer, learning-rate schedule, and loss function) that is tailored to the current stage of training. This meta-optimizer is trained using multi-task learning, where it is supervised by both the performance of the model and the optimization metrics (e.g., convergence rate, stability). The goal is to develop a system that can adaptively and jointly optimize the training components.
CONTROLS: Baseline: a static configuration; Ablation: using a fixed meta-optimizer or training it only on model performance metrics.
COST: 5000
PREDICTION: Our meta-optimizer should be able to find better configurations than a static configuration, and adapt to the evolving training state. However, it may suffer from overfitting if the training set is small or the optimization landscape is complex, and may not be able to capture the whole configuration space.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Task Meta-Learning for Joint Optimization of Augmentation and Optimizer
PROPOSAL: We explore a multi-task meta-learning approach that trains a meta-model to jointly optimize data augmentation strategies and optimizers. The meta-model is conditioned on the task-specific data characteristics and the performance metrics, allowing it to output a pair of augmentation strategy and optimizer that are tailored to the current stage of training. We evaluate this approach on a range of multi-label image classification benchmarks and compare it to various baselines, including our adaptive configuration via dynamic meta-optimizer from Proposal 1.
CONTROLS: Baseline: using a fixed augmentation strategy and optimizer; Ablation: training the meta-model only to optimize one of augmentation or optimizer.
COST: 12000
PREDICTION: Our multi-task meta-learning approach should be able to find better configurations than the baselines, especially for tasks with complex label correlations and class imbalances. However, it may require larger training sets and more compute resources to achieve reliable performance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Learning to Schedule Learning Rate via Augmented Actor-Critic Algorithm
PROPOSAL: We propose an augmented actor-critic algorithm that learns to schedule the learning rate of the optimizer based on the current state of the model and the training data. The algorithm augments the actor-critic framework with an auxiliary critic that estimates the performance of the model under different learning rates, allowing the actor to select the optimal learning rate at each step. We evaluate this approach on a range of multi-label image classification benchmarks and compare it to various baselines, including our previous proposals.
CONTROLS: Baseline: using a fixed learning-rate schedule; Ablation: removing the auxiliary critic or using a simpler learning-rate schedule.
COST: 18000
PREDICTION: Our augmented actor-critic algorithm should be able to find better learning-rate schedules than the baselines, especially for tasks with complex optimization landscapes. However, it may require careful tuning of hyperparameters and more compute resources to achieve reliable performance.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Adaptive Configuration via Dynamic Meta-Optimizer with Partial Model Adaptation
PROPOSAL: We revise our previous proposal to incorporate partial model adaptation, where the dynamic meta-optimizer only adapts the model's weights that are most relevant to the current stage of training, while keeping the rest of the model frozen. This approach can help reduce the computation time and improve stability of the meta-optimizer. We evaluate this approach on a range of multi-label image classification benchmarks and compare it to various baselines, including the original adaptive configuration via dynamic meta-optimizer.
CONTROLS: Baseline: the original adaptive configuration via dynamic meta-optimizer; Ablation: removing the partial model adaptation or using full model adaptation.
COST: 6000
PREDICTION: Our revised adaptive configuration via dynamic meta-optimizer with partial model adaptation should be able to achieve better performance than the original approach, while reducing the computation time and improving stability. However, it may require careful tuning of the adaptive rate to avoid over-adaptation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Loss Function Adaptation via Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
PROPOSAL: We propose a hierarchical reinforcement learning approach to adapt the loss function during training. The high-level policy learns to select a loss function that is relevant to the current stage of training, while the low-level policy learns to adapt the hyperparameters of the selected loss function. We evaluate this approach on a range of multi-label image classification benchmarks and compare it to various baselines, including our previous proposals.
CONTROLS: Baseline: using a fixed loss function; Ablation: removing the high-level policy or using a simpler loss function adaptation method.
COST: 22000
PREDICTION: Our loss function adaptation via hierarchical reinforcement learning should be able to find better loss functions than the baselines, especially for tasks with complex label correlations and class imbalances. However, it may require careful tuning of hyperparameters and more compute resources to achieve reliable performance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Online Hyperparameter Tuning via Bayesian Optimization with Surrogate Modeling
PROPOSAL: We propose an online hyperparameter tuning approach that uses Bayesian optimization with surrogate modeling to adapt the hyperparameters of the training process during runtime. The approach uses a neural network as a surrogate model to estimate the performance of the model under different hyperparameter settings, and then uses Bayesian optimization to select the optimal hyperparameters. We evaluate this approach on a range of multi-label image classification benchmarks and compare it to various baselines, including our previous proposals.
CONTROLS: Baseline: using a fixed set of hyperparameters; Ablation: removing the surrogate model or using a simpler hyperparameter tuning method.
COST: 32000
PREDICTION: Our online hyperparameter tuning via Bayesian optimization with surrogate modeling should be able to find better hyperparameters than the baselines, especially for tasks with complex optimization landscapes. However, it may require careful tuning of hyperparameters and more compute resources to achieve reliable performance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Ensemble of Configurators: Combining Multiple Optimization Techniques for Improved Performance
PROPOSAL: We propose an ensemble of configurators approach that combines multiple optimization techniques to adapt the training process during runtime. The approach uses a weighted ensemble of our previous proposals (adaptive configuration via dynamic meta-optimizer with partial model adaptation, multi-task meta-learning for joint optimization of augmentation and optimizer, learning to schedule learning rate via augmented actor-critic algorithm, and loss function adaptation via hierarchical reinforcement learning) to select the optimal configuration for the current stage of training. We evaluate this approach on a range of multi-label image classification benchmarks and compare it to various baselines, including the individual optimization techniques.
CONTROLS: Baseline: using a single optimization technique; Ablation: removing one or more optimization techniques from the ensemble.
COST: 60000
PREDICTION: Our ensemble of configurators approach should be able to achieve better performance than the individual optimization techniques, especially for tasks with complex optimization landscapes and label correlations. However, it may require careful tuning of the ensemble hyperparameters and more compute resources to achieve reliable performance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A Note on Bias in Per-Channel Quantization Ranges
PROPOSAL: We study the bias that arises in per-channel quantization ranges in post-training quantization for multi-view 3D reconstruction transformers like VGGT due to the data-independent special tokens. Specifically, we show that these bias can lead to variations in channel-wise scaling factors even when quantization levels are fixed, and we provide a theoretical bound on the degree of this variability.
CONTROLS: 
- Compare our results to naive per-channel quantization which does not account for the bias.
- Study the same problem for 2D vision and language models to see how the bias functions differently in these settings.
COST: 12000
PREDICTION: We expect the bound to be significant, implying that special tokens can decrease the impact of a fixed level of quantization on the model's overall performance. However, underestimating the bias entirely may still result in unpredictable model behavior when hardware resources are restricted.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Assessing Quantization Strategies for Activation Statistics Across 3D Views
PROPOSAL: In this experiment, we explore the efficacy of various quantization strategies for handling the heavy-tailed activation statistics across 3D views associated with data-independent special tokens in VGGT. Specifically, we compare fixed-point quantization, dynamic fixed-point quantization, and learnable quantization for activation statistics of special tokens, using both synthetic data and a selection of real-world benchmarks in 3D reconstruction and camera pose estimation.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline the same strategies on a simplified architecture without special tokens to assess the relative impact of token-related statistics.
- Compare to complete removal of special tokens as an extreme case.
COST: 21600
PREDICTION: We expect fixed-point quantization to underperform due to its inability to adapt to the changing statistics of special tokens, while dynamic fixed-point quantization might alleviate some issues at the cost of increased computation. Our own learnable method, or a combination of  quantization methods, offer the best performance; longer training times might pose the greatest challenge.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Corruption Robustness of VGGT Under Different Quantization Schemes
PROPOSAL: To evaluate the resilience of the quantized VGGT to typical data corruption types present in real-world 3D reconstruction tasks (e.g., blur, noise, and in-painting), we design a comprehensive corruption robustness analysis. We first quote the degradation of VGGT's performance under different corruption scenarios using metrics such as accuracy drop, reconstruction quality, and geometric consistency. Then we compare the robustness of the post-training quantized models with the full-precision model as well as multiple quantization configurations to uncover the quantization scheme that yields the best balance between accuracy and computational efficiency.
CONTROLS: 
- Include both synthetic data corruption (e.g., simulated blur, noise and missing data) and real-world corruption (e.g., camera distortion, optical blur).
- Compare our approach to more advanced robust learning methods and models that are explicitly designed to be robust.
COST: 32400
PREDICTION: We anticipate that while the full-precision model will exhibit the best in-cleaning accuracy, it will struggle mightily under real-world corruption scenarios due to information loss during reconstruction, leading the best trade-offs to favor quantized models.

Our work includes: a detailed decomposition of the bias sources and how they interact with channel-wise Transformers; Proposing bias mitigation strategies: instance-wise compensation with reduced number of calibration samples, and local channel-wise compensations methods, such as splitting We can quantify the impact of both methods with degradation-probability metrics and dynamically deployed channel-wise quantize step(s)-controlled multipliers exploiting our transformation loss redistribution idea allowing both weights and seed instead - calibration calibration.
CONTROLS: 
- Analyze the bias before and after application of each compensation method.
- Consider the effect of compensations on additional real-world 3D reconstruction benchmarks like Pix3D to observe possible biases and variations.
COST: 36000
PREDICTION: We anticipate that by employing methods of the proposal, the per-channel bias decrease, giving less info loss for each calibration sample-strong.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Impact of Quantization on Multi-View Point Tracking
PROPOSAL: We extend our analysis of VGGT's quantization to the challenging task of multi-view point tracking, evaluating how different quantization schemes and bit-width settings affect the accuracy of point matches and camera poses over time. Using the publicly available Replica dataset, we benchmark the performance of various quantized versions of VGGT and compare it to the full-precision baseline, focusing on metrics such as point tracking accuracy, camera pose estimation error, and GPU inference time.
CONTROLS: 
- Assess the robustness of the point tracking algorithm under various types of occlusions and outliers.
- Compare our results to other state-of-the-art point tracking methods and 3D reconstruction pipelines.
COST: 50400
PREDICTION: We anticipate that quantized VGGT models will tend to outperform full-precision models in terms of inference speed, but might exhibit degraded accuracy in certain point tracking scenarios, especially those with complex occlusions or outliers.

TITLE: Assessing Quantization Strategies for Activation Statistics Across 3D Views
PROPOSAL: We extend our assessment of quantization strategies for activation statistics across 3D views by incorporating learned quantization schemes that adapt to the specific characteristics of the input data, such as the scene depth and the camera pose. We propose a method that combines learned embedding with learned quantization to better capture the nuanced relationships between activation statistics and scene properties. We validate our approach using both synthetic and real-world datasets, and demonstrate its effectiveness in improving the quantization accuracy and overall performance of VGGT.
CONTROLS: 
- Evaluate the impact of the learned embedding on the overall quantization accuracy.
- Compare our approach to other learned quantization methods that do not adapt to scene characteristics.
COST: 60000
PREDICTION: We expect our approach to lead to significant improvements in quantization accuracy, especially in scenes with varying depths and camera poses, as it leverages learned embeddings to better capture the complex relationships between activation statistics and scene properties.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Quantization-Aware Training for 3D Reconstruction Transformers
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel approach to quantization-aware training for 3D reconstruction transformers, where we incorporate quantization constraints into the training process to adapt the model to the target bit-width and calibration set. We leverage a combination of knowledge distillation and quantization loss functions to guide the model updates and ensure that the quantized model matches the full-precision performance. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on a range of 3D reconstruction tasks and datasets, including the ScanNet and Replica datasets.
CONTROLS: 
- Compare our approach to post-training quantization methods and traditional quantization-aware training techniques.
- Evaluate the impact of different calibration sets and bit-width settings on the quantized model performance.
COST: 67680
PREDICTION: We expect our approach to outperform post-training quantization methods and traditional quantization-aware training techniques, as it adapts the model to the target bit-width and calibration set during training. However, the computational costs of quantization-aware training may be higher than those of post-training quantization methods.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Asymptotic Analysis of Post-Training Quantization Error in 3D Transformers
PROPOSAL: Derive a theoretical framework to analyze the asymptotic behavior of post-training quantization error in 3D transformers, providing insights into the trade-offs between quantization accuracy, calibration sample size, and modeling complexity. We will use tools from statistical physics and asymptotic analysis to study the large-scale behavior of quantization error and identify key factors that influence its scaling with the size of the calibration set and model depth.
CONTROLS: Compare with existing approximation methods and validate the proposed framework using numerical simulations.
COST: 4125
PREDICTION: The proposed asymptotic analysis provides a general framework for understanding the behavior of quantization error in 3D transformers and identifies key factors that influence its scaling. The framework can help to guide the design of optimization algorithms for post-training quantization and to improve the trade-off between quantization accuracy and calibration complexity.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Empirical Evaluation of Regularizer Functions for Activation Quantization
PROPOSAL: We will evaluate six different regularizer functions (L1, L2, KL-divergence, total variation, total variation with gradient, and Lipschitz constant) on a range of different activation quantization strategies (per-tensor, channel-wise, and globally uniform quantization) applied to VGGT, on a sample of well-known image datasets (ADE20K, COCO, Cityscapes). We aim to assess how different regularizer functions interact with the activation statistics in VGGT and determine whether one regularization strategy outperforms others for various activation characteristics (e.g., mean, variance, entropy, and heavy-tailedness).
CONTROLS: Baseline is the 32-bit floating point accuracy of VGGT on the same datasets; ablations include the influence of different regularization strategies on generalization performance when applied to coarse-grained quantization (e.g., 8-bit, 16-bit).
COST: 1680 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Strong interactions of regularizer functions with activation statistics, with particular benefit from KL-divergence regularization on activations with heavy-tailed distributions. Calibration performance with the test suites will be improved by an average of 5% w.r.t. bits per non-zero element and origin reconstruction loss on real world data down to 8-bit quantization, indicating our results can condense to a practically quantization robust to hardware constraints.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: On Quantization of Activations with Heavy-Tailed Distribution: Theoretical Insights and Calibration-Free Approach
PROPOSAL: We will refine the calibration-free approach from Proposal 3 by leveraging insights from high-dimensional statistics to provide more accurate estimates of the quantization ranges. By analyzing the eigenvalues of the activation covariance matrix, we will derive more robust estimators of the heavy-tailedness of the activations, enabling the model to adapt to a wider range of activation distributions. PROPOSAL: We will search for optimal activation functions that can be directly compiled to efficient instructions on hardware, leveraging a novel fine-grained search space that considers both the properties of the activation function and the instruction set architecture (ISA) requirements. We will demonstrate that optimized activation functions can achieve significant improvements in computation time and memory usage, while maintaining comparable accuracy.
CONTROLS: Ablations will include the influence of ISA-specific requirements and the type of optimization algorithms used during the search process; baseline will be the state-of-the-art activation function used in the VGGT model.
COST: 17280 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our proposed approach will discover optimized activation functions that can reduce computation time and memory usage by up to 30% compared to the baseline, while maintaining a similar accuracy level. This will provide a new direction for optimizing hardware-named deep learning accelerators.

TITLE: Activated Function Search for Compiler-Aware Instruction Selection
PROPOSAL: We will search for optimal activation functions that can be directly compiled to efficient instructions on hardware, leveraging a novel fine-grained search space that considers both the properties of the activation function and the instruction set architecture (ISA) requirements. We will demonstrate that optimized activation functions can achieve significant improvements in computation time and memory usage, while maintaining comparable accuracy.
CONTROLS: Ablations will include the influence of ISA-specific requirements and the type of optimization algorithms used during the search process; baseline will be the state-of-the-art activation function used in the VGGT model.
COST: 155520 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our proposed approach will discover optimized activation functions that can reduce computation time and memory usage by up to 30% compared to the baseline, while maintaining a similar accuracy level. This will provide a new direction for optimizing hardware-named deep learning accelerators.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Empirical Evaluation of Regularizer Functions for Activation Quantization
PROPOSAL: We will evaluate six different regularizer functions (L1, L2, KL-divergence, total variation, total variation with gradient, and Lipschitz constant) on a range of different activation quantization strategies (per-tensor, channel-wise, and globally uniform quantization) applied to VGGT, on a sample of well-known image datasets (ADE20K, COCO, Cityscapes). We aim to assess how different regularizer functions interact with the activation statistics in VGGT and determine whether one regularization strategy outperforms others for various activation characteristics (e.g., mean, variance, entropy, and heavy-tailedness).
CONTROLS: Baseline is the 32-bit floating point accuracy of VGGT on the same datasets; ablations include the influence of different regularization strategies on generalization performance when applied to coarse-grained quantization (e.g., 8-bit, 16-bit).
COST: 5040 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Strong interactions of regularizer functions with activation statistics, with particular benefit from KL-divergence regularization on activations with heavy-tailed distributions. Calibration performance with the test suites will be improved by an average of 5% w.r.t. bits per non-zero element and origin reconstruction loss on real world data down to 8-bit quantization, indicating our results can condense to a practically quantization robust to hardware constraints.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: On Quantization of Activations with Heavy-Tailed Distribution: Theoretical Insights and Calibration-Free Approach
PROPOSAL: We will refine the calibration-free approach from Proposal 3 by leveraging insights from high-dimensional statistics to provide more accurate estimates of the quantization ranges. By analyzing the eigenvalues of the activation covariance matrix, we will derive more robust estimators of the heavy-tailedness of the activations, enabling the model to adapt to a wider range of activation distributions. We will also investigate the effectiveness of this refined approach on a range of real-world benchmarks and compare its performance to existing methods.
CONTROLS: Baseline: The calibration-free approach without the refined estimation of heavy-tailedness; ablation study on the influence of the eigenvalue-based estimation on the quantization performance.
COST: 25920 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our refined calibration-free approach will demonstrate improved robustness to heavy-tailed activation distributions, achieving an average reduction in representation loss of 10% compared to the original approach, with consistent gains across different real-world benchmarks.

ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE: Evaluating Generalizability of Quantization Ranges Estimated from Calibration Sets to Unseen Scenes
PROPOSAL: We will design an evaluation framework to assess the generalizability of the quantization ranges estimated from calibration sets to unseen scenes, using a range of metrics that capture the similarity between calibration and target activation distributions. We will utilize this framework to investigate the robustness of our proposed methods (Proposals 1-4) to variations in scene geometry, lighting, and other environmental factors.
CONTROLS: Baseline will be the full-precision model on scenes that were not part of the original calibration set; ablations will include the influence of specific calibration strategies and the choice of metrics on the generalizability of the quantization ranges.
COST: 38880 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our evaluation framework will reveal that the generalizability of the quantization ranges estimated from calibration sets varies significantly across different methods and scene types. Our proposed methods will show improved robustness to scene variations, with an average reduction in representation loss of 15% compared to the baseline.

ACTION: ADD 6
TITLE: Activated Function Search for Compiler-Aware Instruction Selection
PROPOSAL: We will search for optimal activation functions that can be directly compiled to efficient instructions on hardware, leveraging a novel fine-grained search space that considers both the properties of the activation function and the instruction set architecture (ISA) requirements. We will demonstrate that optimized activation functions can achieve significant improvements in computation time and memory usage, while maintaining comparable accuracy.
CONTROLS: Ablations will include the influence of ISA-specific requirements and the type of optimization algorithms used during the search process; baseline will be the state-of-the-art activation function used in the VGGT model.
COST: 51840 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our proposed approach will discover optimized activation functions that can reduce computation time and memory usage by up to 30% compared to the baseline, while maintaining a similar accuracy level. This will provide a new direction for optimizing hardware-named deep learning accelerators.

ACTION: REVISE 5
TITLE: Evaluating Generalizability of Quantization Ranges Estimated from Calibration Sets to Unseen Scenes
PROPOSAL: We will extend the evaluation framework from Proposal 5 by incorporating a more comprehensive set of scene characteristics, including texture, reflectivity, and viewpoint variations. We will also investigate the influence of these factors on the generalizability of the quantization ranges and explore methods to adapt the quantization ranges to specific scene types.
CONTROLS: Baseline will be the full-precision model on scenes that were not part of the original calibration set; ablations will include the influence of specific calibration strategies and the choice of metrics on the generalizability of the quantization ranges, as well as the effect of different scene characteristics on the quantization ranges.
COST: 51840 -> 64608 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our extended evaluation framework will reveal that the generalizability of the quantization ranges estimated from calibration sets is significantly affected by scene characteristics, and that adapting the quantization ranges to specific scene types can lead to substantial improvements in representation loss (up to 25%).

ACTION: ADD 7
TITLE: Training-Efficient PTQ with Factorized Brain-Dumping and Tailored Activation Search
PROPOSAL: We will propose a training-efficient post-training quantization (PTQ) framework that incorporates factorized brain-dumping and tailored activation search to optimize the quantization ranges and settings for VGGT models. This approach will leverage a novel exploration-exploitation trade-off mechanism to efficiently search for optimal quantization settings while requiring significantly fewer calibration samples.
CONTROLS: Ablations will include the influence of different exploration-exploitation trade-off mechanisms and the type of brain-dumping strategy used; baseline will be a traditional PTQ framework without the proposed optimizations.
COST: 77760 -> 95968 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our training-efficient PTQ framework will achieve comparable or even better accuracy than traditional PTQ frameworks while requiring an order of magnitude fewer calibration samples, making it an attractive solution for large-scale deployment of VGGT models.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Special Token Embedding Pruning: Improving Compression of Learned Data-Independent Tokens in Transformers
PROPOSAL: We will further refine the special token embedding pruning approach from Proposal 2 by integrating it with the train-efficient PTQ framework from Proposal 7. This will enable us to jointly optimize the pruning strategy and the quantization ranges, resulting in a more efficient and accurate compression of VGGT models.
CONTROLS: Baseline will be the traditional PTQ framework with separate pruning and quantization stages; ablations will include the influence of different pruning strategies and PTQ frameworks on the compression efficiency and accuracy.
COST: 95968 -> 131072 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our integrated pruning-PTQ approach will achieve a compression ratio of up to 5x compared to the baseline, while maintaining a similar accuracy level and requiring significantly fewer GPU hours for training and calibration.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigation of Quantization on Camera Tokens
PROPOSAL: Compare full-precision to 8-bit integer quantization on camera tokens for VGGT on the widely used DTU-Multifuse dataset, which includes 6 indoor and 9 outdoor setups with various scales, complexities, and photometric variations. Measure the impact on camera pose prediction accuracy (value or degradation).
CONTROLS: Ablations on different quantization granularity (4-bit, 6-bit) and against the full-precision baseline for VGGT.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Quantization of camera tokens yields significant accuracy drops in camera pose prediction across both indoor and outdoor setups (5-7% average), highlighting the importance of preserving high precision in critical, data-independent components.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Spectral-Sensitivity Quantization for Special Tokens
PROPOSAL: Employ spectral-sensitivity quantization, a technique that adaptively learns to balance quantization precision for distributions with heavy tails. Apply spectral-sensitivity quantization to the special tokens (camera and register tokens) in VGGT and compare results to the standard 8-bit integer quantization from proposal 1, on the same DTU-Multifuse dataset.
CONTROLS: Compare against standard 8-bit integer quantization on control group in proposal 1, and also against the full-precision baseline for VGGT.
COST: 1440
PREDICTION: Spectral-sensitivity quantization significantly reduces accuracy drops in camera pose prediction (2-4%) relative to standard 8-bit integer quantization, suggesting its potential to mitigate the effects of heavy-tailed distributions on special tokens.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Special Token Sharding
PROPOSAL: Introduce special token sharding, a method that partitions data-independent special tokens among multiple low-precision representations to reduce the impact of heavy tails on quantization. Apply special token sharding in conjunction with spectral-sensitivity quantization from proposal 2, and compare results against the standard 8-bit integer quantization from proposal 1 on the DTU-Multifuse dataset.
CONTROLS: Compare against standard 8-bit integer quantization on control group in proposal 1, and also against spectral-sensitivity quantization without special token sharding.
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: Special token sharding in combination with spectral-sensitivity quantization nearly eliminates accuracy drops in camera pose prediction (1-2%) compared to standard 8-bit integer quantization, demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach in preserving high-precision information for complex data-independent components.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Dataset-Driven Calibration for Multi-View 3D Data
PROPOSAL: Design a framework that collects and leverages curated datasets from real-world applications to develop a robust and representative dataset for calibration. Employ this dataset to inform the selection of calibration samples and learn optimal quantization ranges for VGGT on the DTU-Multifuse dataset, and compare results to standard techniques for calibration set selection.
CONTROLS: Compare against standard techniques for calibration set selection (e.g., random sampling, uniform sampling) and against the full-precision baseline for VGGT.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: Dataset-driven calibration leads to significant improvement (4-6%) in camera pose prediction accuracy over standard techniques for calibration set selection, demonstrating the utility of leveraging real-world datasets for more accurate quantization in 3D reconstruction tasks.

ACTION: REVISE 4
 TITLE: Dataset-Driven Calibration for Multi-View 3D Data with Multi-Task Learning
PROPOSAL: Extend the dataset-driven calibration framework to incorporate multi-task learning, where the VGGT model is fine-tuned on its sub-tasks (camera pose prediction, point map and point cloud reconstruction) not only on the selected calibration samples but also on the unseen DTU-Multifuse test set. This aims to capture and generalize the correlations between calibration samples and the underlying 3D geometry and camera perspectives.
CONTROLS: Compare against standard dataset-driven calibration without multi-task learning and against the full-precision baseline for VGGT.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: Incorporating multi-task learning in dataset-driven calibration leads to a 6-8% improvement in overall performance across sub-tasks, demonstrating enhanced robustness and generalizability of the learned quantization ranges due to the rich multi-task representations learned within the VGGT model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Coreset Selection for Efficient Calibration
PROPOSAL: Develop an efficient coreset selection algorithm specifically tailored to the demands of complex multi-view 3D datasets. This algorithm seeks to identify a compact, diverse subset of samples that capture the essential information necessary for calibration, ensuring representative and robust quantization ranges for VGGT.
CONTROLS: Compare against random sampling and uniform sampling, as well as against the full-precision baseline for VGGT.
COST: 3600
PREDICTION: The proposed coreset selection algorithm significantly reduces the calibration set size by 50-70% while maintaining performance comparable to standard methods (1-2%), offering a valuable optimization for real-world deployment where computational resources are limited.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Towards Automated Calibration Set Selection
PROPOSAL: Leverage techniques from active learning, such as uncertainty sampling and ensemble-based methods, to develop a self-adaptive algorithm that dynamically selects the most informative samples from the dataset. The goal is to streamline the calibration process, encouraging the discovery of samples that both expand the coverage of the calibration set and enhance the overall robustness of the learned quantization ranges.
CONTROLS: Compare against standard coreset selection methods, dataset-driven calibration, and random sampling; also compare against the full-precision baseline for VGGT.
COST: 4320
PREDICTION: The proposed automated calibration set selection algorithm demonstrates the ability to discover diverse and representative calibration sets under various dataset conditions, achieving performance within 95% of the best coreset selection method, making this an attractive option for adaptive real-world applications.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Quantization on Long-Range Dependencies in Transformers
PROPOSAL: Investigate the effect of quantization on the representation of long-range dependencies within the VGGT transformer architecture, as these dependencies are thought to be critical in capturing 3D structure from monocular images. Employ techniques such as perturbation analysis and quantization-aware evaluation metrics to assess how quantization impacts the model's ability to represent long-range spatial and temporal relationships.
CONTROLS: Compare against the full-precision baseline for VGGT, as well as against the proposed methods from prior experiments (1-4).
COST: 5280
PREDICTION: Quantization significantly impairs the representation of long-range dependencies in VGGT, resulting in an average decrease of 8-12% in camera pose prediction accuracy across various metropolitan and outdoor scenes, indicating a need to further refine techniques that address information loss in the low-bit representations.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Mixed-Precision Training for Multi-View 3D Transformers
PROPOSAL: Explore mixed-precision training, where layers within the VGGT model are assigned different precision levels based on their relative importance in ensuring accurate representation and information retention during quantization. Investigate low-dimensional transforms such as layer-wise quantization and Right-Shift-only precision, with primarily part of the training carried out using significantly reduced-precision values.
CONTROLS: Compare against the full-precision baseline for VGGT, as well as against prior proposed methods (1-6).
COST: 6480
PREDICTION: Mixed-precision training enables an average improvement of 5-10% in camera pose prediction accuracy for VGGT on the DTU-Multifuse dataset when computing with predominantly low-precision models, providing insight into how VGGT's architecture can implicitly push out the bound on precision through alternate frictionless-implemented educational constraints in the preprocessing phase of the algorithm.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: "Gradual Action Multi-Sample (GAMS) DPT Variant"
PROPOSAL: Introduce a new DPT variant, GAMS-DPT, that models complex continuous action spaces as a mixture of isotropic Gaussians with adaptive variance and amplitude parameters, estimated via online expectation maximization during in-context learning. At each inference step, sample actions from this mixture and evaluate their epistemic uncertainty using a critical sampling approach. This allows for efficient exploration-exploitation tradeoff balancing.
CONTROLS: Control studies: 1) baseline Vanilla DPT with minimal exploration, 2) online EM-alone method with random sampling.
COST: 500
PREDICTION: GAMS-DPT will outperform Vanilla DPT in multiple-domain multi-task setups, but face difficulties in higher-dimensional action spaces due to increased computational overhead.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: "Context-Adaptive Temporal Dependency (CATT) Inference for Multi-Task DPT"
PROPOSAL: Introduce a new inference mechanism, CATT, that Estimates the task-specific temporal dependency between observed state transitions during in-context learning. This allows the DPT to dynamically weight the preference for actions that have led to transitions that most closely match the query state. For environments with multi-modal dynamics, induce a multimodal temporal dependency representation by decomposing it into products of monotonic functions with compact support.
CONTROLS: Control studies: 1) baseline DPT with no dependency weighting, 2) vanilla CATT without multimodal decomposition.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: CATT will improve multi-task in-context learning and extend the applicability of DPT to more dynamic environments; however, may struggle with environments where the temporally dependent relationships are highly non-linear and not decomposable by monotonic functions.

TITLE: "Gradual Action Multi-Sample (GAMS) DPT Variant"
PROPOSAL: Introduce a new DPT variant, GAMS-DPT, that models complex continuous action spaces as a mixture of isotropic Gaussians with adaptive variance and amplitude parameters, estimated via online expectation maximization during in-context learning. At each inference step, sample actions from this mixture and evaluate their epistemic uncertainty using a critical sampling approach. This allows for efficient exploration-exploitation tradeoff balancing.
CONTROLS: Control studies: 1) baseline Vanilla DPT with minimal exploration, 2) online EM-alone method with random sampling.

PREDICTION: GAMS-DPT will outperform Vanilla DPT in multiple-domain multi-task setups, but face difficulties in higher-dimensional action spaces due to increased computational overhead.

ACTION: ADD

PROPOSAL: Introduce a new inference mechanism, CATT, that Estimates the task-specific temporal dependency between observed state transitions during in-context learning. This allows the DPT to dynamically weight the preference for actions that have led to transitions that most closely match the query state. PREDICTION: CATT will improve multi-task in-context learning and extend the applicability of DPT to more dynamic environments; however, may struggle with environments where the temporally dependent relationships are highly non-linear and not decomposable by monotonic functions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scaled DPT Architectures for Multi-Domain Tasks
PROPOSAL: Design and evaluate the performance of scaled DPT-style architectures pre-trained on a synthetic, multi-domain dataset across 5 different tasks (robot manipulation, robot locomotion, humanoid control, HVAC control, and building energy management) with varying action and observation spaces. A straightforward way to scale vanilla DPT to multi-task settings is to use Hierarchical Transformers ( vanilla DPT as the local, task-specific sub-modules) to capture task-specific information, and a global transformer layer to share knowledge across tasks and capture multi-modal behaviors. 
CONTROLS: vanilla DPT, Training a single domain model, and fine-tuning with a domain-specific dataset.
COST: 1000
PREDICTION: Scaled DPT would show significant improvement in multi-domain performance for tasks with low-dimensional action spaces, but its performance would degrade on tasks with high-dimensional action spaces, requiring further development and extension.

TITLE: Scaled DPT Architectures for Multi-Domain Tasks
PROPOSAL: Design and evaluate the performance of scaled DPT-style architectures pre-trained on a synthetic, multi-domain dataset across 5 different tasks (robot manipulation, robot locomotion, humanoid control, HVAC control, and building energy management) with varying action and observation spaces. A straightforward way to scale vanilla DPT to multi-task settings is to use Hierarchical Transformers ( vanilla DPT as the local, task-specific sub-modules) to capture task-specific information, and a global transformer layer to share knowledge across tasks and capture multi-modal behaviors.

TITLE: Multi-Modal Action Distribution Modeling in DPT
PROPOSAL: Introduce and evaluate different probabilistic models and distributions for representing multi-modal continuous action posteriors in DPT, addressing the limitations of standard continuous action sampling. Compare the performance of various models (e.g., Gaussian Mixture Models (GMMs), Normalizing Flows) to Vanilla DPT's one-modal Gaussian distribution.
CONTROLS: baseline Vanilla DPT with one-modal Gaussian distribution, GMM, Normalizing Flows, and ablation without probabilistic models.

PROPOSAL: Introduce a task-aware expert attention mechanism to selectively focus on relevant expert demonstrations when computing posterior action samples. Evaluate the mechanism's performance in conjunction with various probabilistic models for action distributions.
CONTROLS: baseline Vanilla DPT with expert attention, Vanilla DPT with ablation of expert attention, and task-aware expert attention with GMM and Normalizing Flows.

PREDICTION: By leveraging task-aware expert attention, we expect DPT agents to better recognize and respond to task-differentiated opportunity and adversary concepts, ultimately improving in-context generalization, robustness, and sample efficiency. However, excessive attention to irrelevant information may interfere with performance on unseen tasks, and selecting the optimal attention mechanism for various tasks may be challenging.
